articles.title: Phil Parkinson: Wrexham had to block outside noise
articles.summary: Wrexham had to "block everything out"  says Phil Parkinson as they responded to recent criticism with a victory over Preston North End.
articles.body:
Manager Phil Parkinson says Wrexham had to "block everything out" as they responded to recent criticism with a convincing 4-1 Championship victory over Preston North End at the Racecourse.

Wrexham returned to winning ways after suffering a disappointing 2-1 home defeat by West Bromwich Albion in midweek.

Reports suggesting pressure was beginning to mount on Parkinson following a slow start to the campaign.

"I have managed over 1,000 games so I'm used to that," Parkinson told BBC Radio Wales Sport.

"When you lose at any level, criticism comes the manager's way and the players' way and you've got to accept that.

"Obviously the criticism of Wrexham is intensified because of the profile of the club."

First goals for the club from Joe Worrall and Ben Whiteman helped Wrexham establish a 2-1 half-time lead.

Sam Smith and Kieffer Moore's second half goals completed an emphatic victory over the Championship's bottom side.

"We couldn't wait to get back out here today," Parkinson said.

"I look at it as a challenge. Me and Steve [Parkin] were itching to get back in with the lads on Thursday and bring the group together.

"We thought long and hard about the team selection and the style of play we needed to implement.

"Sometimes you've got to block everything out and put in a performance like we did today.

"I'm very confident we've got a squad that can be really competitive this season. I really am."

Parkinson also pointed to an extensive injury list as a major factor in Wrexham's inconsistent start, with players including Max Cleworth, Nathan Broadhead and Dan Sheaf currently sidelined.

"I don't want to keep going on about the injuries, but it's been unprecedented, probably the worst spell we've had in my time here.

"We've lost a lot of quality and football ability on the pitch.

"But those players will come back and we'll have great competition for places. I really believe in this group.

"While we're waiting for those players to return, it's about galvanising the squad and finding ways to be more effective."

images.caption: Image caption, Wrexham's victory over Preston was their second home win of the season

articles.title: Bellerín: "Hay dos jugadas dudosas y una la castiga y otra la premia"
articles.standfirst: El lateral del Betis quiso quitarle al árbitro "la responsabilidad del resultado"
articles.summary: El lateral del Betis quiso quitarle al árbitro "la responsabilidad del resultado"
articles.body: Héctor Bellerín fue uno de los jugadores del Betis que se pronunció ante los medios tras la derrota frente al Barcelona. El lateral fue cuestionado por la actuación del colegiado "Creo que en la primera parte y al inicio de la segunda, dentro de lo difícil que es defender a un equipo del nivel del Barcelona, las oportunidades han estado repartidas. Ha habido cierto control del balón y no estaba creando lo suficiente un equipo de esa calidad. Luego hay un par de decisiones injustas para ambos lados: una mano que viene de un empujón y un juego peligroso. Y no se castigan de la misma forma", comenzaba el jugador. "La expulsión es una jugada que no nos podemos permitir. He hablado con Facundo y sabe su responsabilidad que tiene y ha pedido perdón al equipo. A partir de ahí, enfrentarte a un equipo de esa calidad con uno menos es una tarea difícil, pero le hemos plantado cara hasta los minutos finales. Con once hemos demostrado que podemos competir contra los equipos de arriba. Como siempre decimos, contra todo y contra todos", señaló en declaraciones a Movistar LaLiga. El catalán quiso rebajar la tensión: "Siempre digo que el trabajo del árbitro es muy difícil y lo último que quiero es darle la responsabilidad del resultado. Para nada es así, pero hay dos jugadas dudosas y una la castiga y otra la premia. Perdemos nosotros, pero jugadas así que son de goles en partido de este calibre... Tenemos que responsabilizarnos de lo que hemos hecho bien y mal. No quiero excusarme en estas injusticias. Hay que sacar energía para salir adelante y mirar de frente a lo que viene". Y de nuevo hacía referencia a la expulsión de Facundo. "En el vestuario hay plena confianza para decirnos las cosas buenas y malas. Todos cometemos errores. Hay que salir a arreglarlo en el próximo partido, con cabeza fría y demostrando la ambición, la energía y las ganas que tiene este equipo para que todo esto que hemos hecho hasta ahora no se quede reflejado en esa acción. Hay que seguir todos juntos. Estamos haciendo una campaña muy grande y tenemos que seguir ahí arriba", finalizó el jugador del Betis.

images.caption: Bellerín celebra un gol con el Betis. MARCA

articles.title: Football gossip: Gyokeres, Rabiot, De Jong, Kounde, Nmecha
articles.summary: Viktor Gyokeres wants to leave Arsenal, Xabi Alonso eyes Barcelona duo and Liverpool target Dortmund's Felix Nmecha.
articles.body:
Viktor Gyokeres wants to leave Arsenal , Xabi Alonso eyes Barcelona duo and Liverpool target Dortmund's Felix Nmecha.

Sweden forward Viktor Gyokeres, 28, is set to push for a move away from Arsenal in the January transfer window because of a lack of playing time. ( TeamTalk , external )

Liverpool are keeping an eye on Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha, 26, if they are unable to secure midfielder Alex Scott, 23, from Bournemouth . (CaughtOffside) , external

AC Milan are preparing to offer French midfielder Adrien Rabiot a new contract until 2030 after the 31-year-old's impressive start to the season. (Corriere dello Sport - in Italian) , external

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is looking to strengthen the depth of his squad in January with two signings from Barcelona in French defender Jules Kounde, 27, and Dutch midfielder Frenkie de Jong, 29. (Football365) , external

Chelsea are also interested in Borussia Dortmund and USA 17-year-old winger Mathis Albert, who has made just one appearance for the German side. ( FootballTransfers , external )

AS Roma and Brazil defender Wesley, 23, has been getting interest from Arsenal , Manchester United and Newcastle . ( SportWitness , external )

Former Brighton defender Solly March, 32, is set to join Championship side Charlton on a free. The Englishman has been out of contract since he was released by the Seagulls in July. (Football Insider) , external

IFK Goteborg 's 17-year-old Swedish midfielder Oliver Mansson has attracted interest from Arsenal and Chelsea . (TeamTalk) , external

Arsenal and Manchester United have ruled out any interest in Sporting and Uruguay left-back Maxi Araujo, 26. (Sport Witness) , external

Chelsea are in advanced talks to sign Moroccan winger Gessime Yassine, 20, from Strasbourg . (Ekrem Konur) , external

articles.title: Arch Manning struggles, Colin Simmons injured as Florida scores 24 straight to upset No. 7 Texas
articles.summary: The Longhorns lost a 14-point lead and fell to an unranked Gators team quarterbacked by a backup making his first career start.
articles.body:
Late in the second quarter Saturday at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium, No. 7 Texas was up 14 points on a Florida team in free fall. The Gators, ranked as high as No. 8 earlier this month, were coming off back-to-back blowout losses, the second of which was handed to them by a South Carolina squad that was previously winless in SEC competition.

To top it off, Florida arrived in Austin with its QB1 nursing a shoulder injury that he suffered in that disheartening setback to the Gamecocks.

With Aaron Philo only available as an emergency backup, sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. got his first career start. Despite the hostile environment and the two-score hole, Jones emerged victorious on the road against the suddenly reeling Longhorns.

The Jones-led Gators dominated the "middle eight," pairing a quick touchdown drive before intermission with a much longer one after halftime, en route to scoring 24 straight points in a 27-24 win .

For Jon Sumrall's Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC), it was an upset victory. For Steve Sarkisian's Texas (4-2, 1-2), it was an utter letdown. In fact, it marked the Longhorns' largest blown lead at home versus an unranked opponent since 1965, according to ESPN.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning struggled most of the afternoon, a week removed from throwing a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions, including a pick-6, in an agonizing Red River Rivalry defeat to Oklahoma .

Entering the final frame against Florida, Manning was averaging -0.7 air yards per completion, per the ESPN broadcast. Although he wowed while evading and then overcoming pressure to rifle a 62-yard completion to wideout Emmett Mosley V — a gain that set up a 9-yard TD pass to Cam Coleman — he fumbled on a potential game-winning drive the next series.

To make matters worse for the Longhorns, their star pass rusher, Colin Simmons, suffered a lower-leg injury in the fourth quarter and didn't return. Simmons began the day with a nation-leading 9.5 sacks and added one more to his total.

He's a heralded NFL Draft prospect. Manning has been in the past; however, his stock has taken a serious hit this month.

Texas scored on its first two possessions. Florida, meanwhile, started with a pair of three-and-outs.

A 32-yard rushing touchdown from running back Raleek Brown slingshotted the Longhorns to a 7-0 advantage. Florida eventually answered Texas' first-quarter field goal with one of its own in the second frame.

But it didn't take long for the Longhorns to restore their two-score lead, thanks to the elusive Ryan Niblett, who took a Gators punt 63 yards to the house, putting Sarkisian's crew up 17-3.

The pendulum began to swing late in the first half. Manning took a sack — he was sacked five times on the day — then threw into double coverage and nearly was picked by Florida safety Bryce Thornton. Two plays after that, Texas turned the ball over on downs.

Cue the first of the Gators' two game-changing touchdown drives. It was made possible, in part, by a 17-yard completion from Jones to Dallas Wilson on fourth-and-12. The series ended with Jones finding tight end Lacota Dippre for a 7-yard score with 18 seconds left in the half.

After getting the ball back to start the second, Jones orchestrated a 15-play, 69-yard drive, which ended with him stepping up and locating Dippre for his second scoring grab.

That capped an eight-minute series and tied the game 17-17.

Another lengthy Florida drive — spanning 14 plays, 57 yards and 6:31 — amounted in one more Patrick Durkin field goal, a 28-yarder that lifted the Gators to a 20-17 lead.

On Texas' next drive, Manning ran right into 319-pound Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett for a loss of 3 yards on fourth-and-2 from about midfield.

An 11-yard Jadan Baugh TD run gave the Gators some breathing room. Manning closed the gap with his strikes to Mosley and Coleman.

Yet when Manning had a chance to exorcise the late-game demons that haunted him last week in Dallas, he fumbled. A blitzing Myles Graham got home, and Manning lost hold of the rock.

Florida recovered, and its newfound hero, Jones, sealed the win on a keeper. The Gators may have an interesting quarterback decision on their hands. The Longhorns do but for entirely different reasons.

Sarkisian repeated throughout his postgame news conference that he's going to "evaluate everything" offensively.

Manning is part of that "everything," Sarkisian confirmed . So is play-calling, he said when asked about it .

articles.title: Alarma con la lesión de Guruzeta
articles.standfirst: El delantero se hace daño en la rodilla izquierda al poco de saltar al campo
articles.summary: El delantero se hace daño en la rodilla izquierda al poco de saltar al campo
articles.body: El Athletic dejará Mestalla con preocupación. La expedición rojiblanca está pendiente de Guruzeta, que ha tenido que ser sustituido con una aparente lesión en la rodilla izquierda que se produjo tras un mal gesto. El futbolista fue sustituido por Maroan en el minuto 69 cuando sólo 6 minutos antes había entrado al campo por Iñaki Williams. El delantero donostiarra se someterá a pruebas médicas en cuanto regrese el equipo a Bilbao. La mecánica de la lesión no fue nada buena y hasta los jugadores del Valencia reclamaron atención médica. Guruzeta se llevó pronto la mano a la corva de su rodilla después de un mal gesto y una muy mala sensación. La preocupación es evidente porque este tipo de percances suelen derivar en lesiones de gravedad. Guruzeta lo sabe bien, pues en 2019 sufrió una rotura en el ligamento cruzado de la rodilla derecha jugando con el Bilbao Athletic al recalificarse con el filial después de haber jugado ya para el primer equipo.

images.caption: Guruzeta apenas estuvo 6 minutos en el campo. Athletic Club

articles.title: El Castellón saca los colores a Las Palmas pese al cambio de técnico
articles.standfirst: Encaja una dura derrota en el Gran Canaria y no encuentran reacción. La afición terminó protestando contra Ramírez y Directiva.
articles.summary: Los orellut sentencian con dos goles en 4 minutos y amargan el debut de Juan Manuel Rodríguez
articles.body: El estreno de Juan Manuel Rodríguez en el banquillo de la UD Las Palmas terminó de la peor manera posible. El conjunto amarillo cayó por 0-3 ante el Castellón en el Estadio de Gran Canaria, superado durante buena parte del encuentro y sin capacidad para reaccionar cuando el marcador se puso en contra. La derrota, además, estuvo acompañada por las protestas de una afición que terminó mostrando su enfado con la dirección del club. El partido arrancó con ritmo alto y una primera advertencia visitante. Orozco se encontró con un centro desde la derecha y remató al larguero cuando había entrado solo en el área. Las Palmas respondió con presión adelantada y Jefté llegó a marcar, aunque su tanto fue anulado por fuera de juego. Poco después, el delantero probó fortuna desde la frontal, pero su disparo se marchó desviado. La igualdad inicial se rompió al cuarto de hora. Isra Suero ejecutó una falta con un disparo espectacular que adelantó al Castellón y dejó tocado al equipo local. Apenas cuatro minutos después llegó el segundo golpe: los visitantes ejecutaron una jugada ensayada en un saque de esquina y Sienra apareció completamente solo en el segundo palo para rematar a la red. Las malas noticias se acumularon para los amarillos con la lesión de Iñaki González en el minuto 24. El futbolista tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego visiblemente afectado y Enzo Loiodice entró en su lugar. Mientras tanto, el Castellón siguió encontrando espacios y obligó a Caro a realizar una gran intervención para evitar el tercero tras una contra. Iván Jaime, el único destacado de Las Palmas, también probó desde fuera del área, con un disparo que se marchó por encima del larguero. Las Palmas llegó al descanso sin argumentos suficientes para discutir la superioridad visitante. El equipo se marchó a vestuarios con un 0-2 y una sonora pitada de los 15.054 espectadores presentes en el Estadio de Gran Canaria. Juan Manuel Rodríguez movió piezas tras el descanso y la entrada de Elías permitió reorganizar al equipo con una defensa de cuatro, con Abou Bassinga en el centro del campo y Andrés Rodríguez en el lateral izquierdo. Sin embargo, el cambio de dibujo no tuvo el efecto esperado. En el minuto 53, Pablo Santiago hizo el tercero con un centro que se fue cerrando, golpeó en el larguero y acabó dejando el balón a su alcance para marcar. El técnico amarillo trató de buscar soluciones con la entrada de Acimovic y Manu Fuster por Jefté y Abou Bassinga. Más adelante también recurrió a Jesé Rodríguez, que sustituyó a Taisei Miyashiro en el minuto 69. Ninguno de los cambios consiguió cambiar el rumbo de un encuentro en el que Las Palmas apenas encontró claridad en ataque y sufrió para contener las llegadas visitantes. El Castellón, lejos de conformarse con la ventaja, siguió buscando más goles. Caro volvió a intervenir con una parada destacada en el lanzamiento de falta posterior a una acción de Herzog y, en el minuto 83, evitó otro tanto visitante. El guardameta fue uno de los pocos amarillos que impidieron que la derrota adquiriera dimensiones todavía mayores. La frustración fue creciendo en la grada a medida que avanzaban los minutos. En el 77, el público comenzó a corear al unísono «Ramírez, vete ya» y «Directiva, dimisión», en una muestra del descontento por la situación deportiva del equipo. El pitido final confirmó una derrota contundente en el estreno de Juan Manuel Rodríguez. La UD Las Palmas no encontró respuesta a los dos primeros goles del Castellón y terminó encajando un tercero que reflejó las dificultades de una tarde para olvidar. El cambio de entrenador no tuvo el efecto inmediato esperado y el equipo queda obligado a reaccionar tras una actuación que aumentó la preocupación de su afición.

articles.title: Aguirre recupera al 'viejo' Valencia
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Mestalla sigue sin mostrar mejoría y solo la entada de Otorbi dio alguna opción a los locales ante un Athletic al que le faltó ir de verdad a por el partido
articles.summary: El equipo de Mestalla sigue sin mostrar mejoría y solo la entada de Otorbi dio alguna opción a los locales ante un Athletic al que le faltó ir de verdad a por el partido
articles.body: No hay efecto. Otro empate que vale de muy poco. El Valencia no arranca. El efecto Aguirre será a largo plazo o no será. Con el mexicano poco ha cambiado. El equipo juega rematadamente mal y solo los chispazos del chico Otorbi y algunas pinceladas de Javi Guerra logran dar sensación de que el Valencia puede ganar algún partido. De hecho, solo ha ganado uno en toda la temporada y sigue en el pozo de la tabla. El Athletic, por su parte, que llevaba demasiado tiempo sin jugar, dejó escapar una buena oportunidad para llevarse los puntos de Mestalla. Apretó en la primera parte, pero se fue quedando sin opciones reales en la segunda hasta firmar un empate sin pena ni gloria. Empezar pitando a tu delantero no es buena idea. Cierto es que Hugo Duro está en uno de esos momentos en los que lo único que puedes hacer es apretar los dientes y batallar, pero su fallo en Santander no se le había olvidado a Mestalla que desde el calentamiento ya le pitaba a su goleador. Los pitos a Hugo (la que le cayó en el cambio fue tremenda) se extendieron al resto del equipo al ver que el nuevo Valencia de Aguirre se parecía demasiado al viejo Valencia de Corberán. Cero juego, cero ocasiones, cero control, cero de todo. El momento más duro de la primera mitad llegó con un doble recorte de Hugo Rincón a Gayà en la línea de fondo que provocó que el capitán cayera de culo al césped encendiendo la protesta de la grada. Aguirre tardó casi media hora en darse cuenta de que intentar sacar el balón jugado con Tárrega y De Haas no era buena idea. Estuvieron un par de veces cerca de meterse en un lío gordo y el mexicano decidió que balonazos y a pelear en campo rival. Ante ese panorama, el Athletic intentaba aprovechar la debilidad evidente del rival. Robert Navarro, Berenguer y Johaneko se hicieron con la pelota con claridad y casi siempre buscaron a Iñaki Williams que con tres zarpazos fue el que más inquietó a un Dimitrievski poco exigido, pero siempre al límite. A los locales les quedaban muy pocos recursos: un disparo lejano de Raba y alguna arrancada de fogueo, como casi siempre, de Danjuma que lleva más de un año sin marcar un gol. Poco más. Guerra lo intentaba por su cuenta, pero al equipo le faltaban demasiadas cosas. La segunda mitad arrancó con los mismos síntomas. El Athletic dominando y el Valencia en un bloque bajo bastante extremo. En ese escenario apareció una contra llevada por Pepelu que filtró un pase en profundidad para Danjuma. Su jugada soñada al galope, pero que acabó, como siempre, con disparo desviado del neerlandés buscando el segundo palo. Nada nuevo. Con una hora sin cumplirse, Aguirre mandó al banco a sus dos delanteros, Raba y Hugo Duro, metió a Danjuma de nueve y revitalizó las bandas con Otrobi y Rioja. Y claro, la cosa cambió. Las tres primeras arrancadas de chaval conectaron nuevamente a la grada y tuvo el gol en una de ellas bastante clara. Con los cambios los locales cambiaron una barbaridad. El Valencia era otro equipo con llegadas de Rioja y Otorbi que hicieron que el Athletic empezar a temer por el partido por primera vez en la noche. En el nuevo partido fueron saltando a escena personajes hasta el momento inéditos. Uno de ellos, Unai Simón, salvó a los suyos del primer gol haciendo una buena parada a Javi Guerra tras la mejor combinación de los de Aguirre. El campeón del mundo volvió a aparecer otra vez negándole el tanto a Guerra tras otras gran internada de Otorbi.

articles.title: No. 25 Northwestern overcomes late failed fake punt, beats Michigan State on last-second field goal
articles.summary: Despite a risky fake punt, the Wildcats used a clutch special teams play to set up a game-winning drive.
articles.body:
Saturday's game between No. 25 Northwestern and Michigan State came down to the wire.

Wildcats kicker Jackson Kleather nailed a 34-yard field goal with just two seconds left to secure the win.

Northwestern took a risk with its play-calling late in the fourth quarter, and it looked like it would cost them. The Wildcats faced fourth-and-8 on their own 28-yard line with 3:29 left and the score tied 21-21. Northwestern head coach David Braun opted for a fake punt, but the Spartans stopped it.

The Wildcats' defense stepped up. As Michigan State kept the ball on the ground and drained the clock, Northwestern's defense held firm and forced a 37-yard field goal attempt. Northwestern's special teams unit got the block and its offense the ball back. Michigan State had blocked a Northwestern field goal attempt in the second quarter.

Quarterback Aidan Chiles then led a drive to get Northwestern into field goal range. This was a personal game for Chiles, who played for Michigan State for the last two years. He finished 18-of-27 passing for 226 yards in his revenge game. He also had 16 carries for 25 yards and a touchdown.

The Wildcats move to 5-1 and are 2-1 in Big Ten play. Michigan State is now 2-5 and has dropped five straight games.

Spartans head coach Pat Fitzgerald also had a personal stake in the one. Fitzgerald coached football at Northwestern from 2006-2022. He is in his first season at the helm of Michigan State and is still searching for his first conference win.

Northwestern returns home next week to host Rutgers. Michigan State will go on the road to face No. 12 UCLA.

articles.title: La tarde más movida de Lamine
articles.standfirst: El 10 del Barça fue protagonista y acabó siendo el blanco de las críticas en La Cartuja
articles.summary: El 10 del Barça fue protagonista y acabó siendo el blanco de las críticas en La Cartuja
articles.body: Lamine Yamal vive, de manera permanente, con los focos apuntando hacia su figura. Es estrella, absoluto protagonista allá por donde pisa y el principal futbolista al que apuntan las miradas en todos los estadios en los que juega. Y eso tiene sus consecuencias. La condición habitual de ser estrella es convertirse en el blanco de la ira de la afición rival. Y el jugador del Barça puede apuntar La Cartuja, después de lo vivido ante el Betis, como uno de esos lugares donde no despierta precisamente simpatía. Lamine pasó por todas las situaciones, vivió todos los estados de ánimo y pisó prácticamente en todos los charcos que aparecieron por el verde de la casa temporal del Betis. La noche empezó a lo grande para el 10. Abrió la veda en un partido frenético con un gol de bandera. Marca de la casa. Salida hacia dentro en conducción y disparo con el interior a la escuadra. Un gol al alcance de muy pocos. En lo puramente futbolístico, Lamine dio un recital. A ese golazo sumó una asistencia a Gabriel Jesus, varios pases de fantasía -Adeyemi falló un mano a mano previo regalo del extremo- y, en definitiva, una actuación más para quitarse el sombrero. El MVP con el que salió bajo el brazo del verde fue más que merecido. Pero hubo más. Mucho más. Lamine propició una de las acciones polémicas del partido. En un pequeño alboroto frente los banquillos, con Valles recriminando a Fermín que permaneciese en el suelo tras el gol de Abde, Lamine apareció pasado de revoluciones para ponerle el cebo a Facundo Bernal, que picó con demasiada facilidad. Del empujó del jugador del Barça se pasó al cabezazo, doble, del centrocampista del Betis. Y los de Pellegrini se quedaron con diez. Mejor para el Barça, imposible. A partir de ahí, La Cartuja la tomó con el extremo. Pitada unánime cada vez que recibía el balón y un punto extra de agresividad en el duelo de los jugadores del Betis cuando Lamine era el objetivo. Cómo lo debió ver Flick que optó por quitar a su estrella cuando el partido, con 2-4, ya estaba resuelto. Vio peligrar el Clásico para su jugador franquicia. Y no había otra salida. La charla del técnico alemán con Lamine tras la sustitución olía a advertencia. A cambio para evitar una posible expulsión que le apartase del Clásico. A medida para calmar las aguas y recetar una dosis de tranquilidad a la grada verdiblanca. Después, el alemán sorteó la pregunta en rueda de prensa con una finta que hubiera firmado su jugador: "Teníamos que cambiar a Lamine era evidente. Le he dicho que estaba orgulloso, que había jugado de forma fantástica". Fue, seguramente, una de las noches más movidas que Lamine ha vivido en su trayectoria como azulgrana. Ya sabe lo que genera, y lo que provoca. Eso sí, dentro de toda esa marejada, el 10 del Barça salió con otros tres puntos en el bolsillo, un gol y una asistencia. Y un claro mensaje con el PSG y el Real Madrid en el horizonte: Lamine se crece en los grandes escenarios.

articles.title: Young star Johan Manzambi proving his worth for rising Aston Villa
articles.summary: Aston Villa are a side back in form, with Johan Manzambi scoring the winner against a Newcastle team he turned down to move to Villa Park.
articles.body:
Johan Manzambi saw first hand how good Aston Villa were last season and is now playing a crucial part in Unai Emery's rebuild in this campaign.

Switzerland midfielder Manzambi, who turned 21 on Wednesday, scored his third goal in Villa colours with the winner in a 1-0 victory over Newcastle - the club he turned down before moving to Villa Park in the summer.

Manzambi played a crucial role in helping Freiburg reach the Europa League final, before the Germans were comprehensively beaten by a Villa side that scored three times in the opening hour on their way to a 3-0 success.

Asked why he had joined Villa, Manzambi said: "The team was very good and I played against them in the final. It's a very good team with a big coach and that was perfect for me."

For Newcastle fans it was one that had got away, as Manzambi had looked set for a move to St James' Park before opting to join Villa in a club record deal of just over £50m.

Manzambi headed in the winner in the north east on Saturday, unmarked eight yards out when found by Joao Gomes' excellent cross.

It comes after he also found the back of the net in the 3-2 win at Tottenham and in the 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

"He has made a very good impact with his qualities," said a delighted Emery. "Skills and intelligence, both he has, and his physicality is very important as well to help us defensively and to help us try to keep the duels offensively.

"So happy he has scored another goal, fantastic for him."

One of the brightest talents in world football

Among players in the Bundesliga in his position last season, Manzambi ranked first for progressive carries of 10 metres or more (116), shot-ending carries (13) and fouls won (78).

He then impressed in the World Cup, scoring twice in the 4-1 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina, getting a goal and an assist in the 2-1 victory over co-hosts Canada and also registering an assist in the 2-0 success over Algeria.

Unfortunately for Manzambi and Switzerland, a knee injury ruled him out of the last-16 penalty shootout win over Colombia and their quarter-final loss to Argentina.

So impressive were his performances last season, that Manzambi finds himself on a 10-man list for the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the world's best player aged under 21.

Also on the shortlist are Spain World Cup winners Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsi, along with Yan Diomande - whose performances earned him a move to Real Madrid, with the winner named on 26 October.

Since his first start for Aston Villa on 19 September against Spurs , only Manchester City 's Erling Haaland - with six - has been involved in more goals among Premier League players in all competitions than Manzambi's five (three goals, two assists).

Team-mate Nicolas Jackson, another to join Villa in the transfer window in a deal worth up to £65m from Chelsea , was quick to praise the youngster.

"He's an amazing player," said Jackson. "He's still growing. Hopefully he can be better and better every game, score goals and assist me as well. Hopefully we work together and achieve many things together.

"He will go a long way and hopefully gets no injuries."

While playing a crucial role in Villa's present and future, the team he has joined is a lot different to the one he played against in the Europa League final.

From the Villa side that won in Istanbul, six of them - goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, defenders Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa, midfielders Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers and striker Ollie Watkins - all left in high-profile moves, while substitutes Harvey Elliott, Jadon Sancho and Leon Bailey are also no longer at the club.

It proved a challenging start to the season for Villa as they only picked up one point from their opening four league games, but this win over Newcastle has extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to five matches.

As well as moving up to 12th in the Premier League, Villa have six points from two ties in the Champions League after thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 on Wednesday and are in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup, where they play at Bournemouth .

How Manzambi became one of Europe's best young talents

Botman challenge 'nearly broke my leg', says Jackson

Jackson has scored five times for Villa since his move and said he was lucky to avoid a serious injury when he was caught in the first half by Newcastle 's Sven Botman, who was only shown a yellow card despite an over-the-ball challenge.

"I know the referee said yellow card but it was so high and hopefully maybe next time a red card, but it was a yellow," said Jackson. "I nearly broke my leg but anyway it's part of football. The most important thing is we win and we won, so I'm OK."

Villa entertain Norwegian side Viking in their third Champions League match of the season on Wednesday before hosting a Manchester City side that have won all seven of their Premier League matches this season.

"It was very important after our poor start [to the season] that we needed to try to come back feeling confident, feeling comfortable in how we are building our structure," added Emery.

"The players themselves tried to be demanding to change the situation where we are.

"Through the [Premier] league we are going to achieve our priority this year, so the league is the competition where we must try to be very consistent."

With seven points from their past three league matches, Villa are a side on the rise again.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Villa content

articles.title: Champions Cup: Munster 33-25 Racing 92 - Southern province win on night they pay tribute to Anthony Foley
articles.summary: Munster start their Champions Cup campaign with a 33-25 win over Racing 92 on an emotional night at Pairc Ui Chaoimh.
articles.body:
Tries: Gleeson, McCarthy, Beirne, F Wycherley, Casey Cons: O'Shea 3, Hanrahan

Tries: Hulleu, Machenaud, Manu Cons: Gibert 2 Pens: Gibert 2

Munster started their Champions Cup campaign with a 33-25 win over Racing 92 on an emotional night at Pairc Ui Chaoimh.

The game was played a decade and a day on from the passing of Munster legend Anthony Foley - the first Munster captain to lift the Heineken Cup - who died in his sleep before a scheduled fixture between these two sides in October 2016.

Before kick-off in Cork, the Shannon RFC choir gave a moving rendition of There is an Isle, the club song that formed such a memorable part of Foley's Limerick funeral.

Neither side took to the field with a player wearing Foley's number eight, while there was also a minute's applause in the eighth minute of a game attended by members of the former Ireland back row's family.

Munster led by 15 points early in the second half after Tadhg Beirne followed first-half tries from Brian Gleeson and Shay McCarthy with a score of his own, but Racing were allowed back into the game.

Second-half tries from Wilfried Hulleu, Maxime Machenaud and Joey Manu, with only Fineen Wycherley crossing in response, had the French outfit within three points going into the final minutes.

Arthur Roche's late yellow card hampered the comeback effort, however, and Craig Casey made the game safe with a try two minutes from time.

Recap: Saturday's Champions Cup action as it happened

Six-try Ulster secure bonus point against Zebre

Seven-try Leinster too strong for Clermont

Three-time beaten finalists in this competition, Racing 92's form across the early weeks of the Top 14 has been indifferent with the Parisians languishing in 12th domestically after four losses in six games.

While they took the lead through an early Antoine Gibert penalty, across a largely listless first half they rarely looked like the side who made it to European showpieces in 2016, 2018 and 2020.

Once the great entertainers on the European scene, this iteration of the side were intent on putting boot to ball early on but got little change from the aerial game.

Gleeson, wearing number 24 for Munster given the absence of the usual number eight jersey, charged off the base of a scrum after six minutes to erase the visitors' early advantage and his side were on top for the remainder of the first half.

McCarthy gathered a somewhat fortuitous bounce before dancing through the visitors' backline for Munster's second score of the evening after only 13 minutes and, in truth, head coach Clayton McMillan will have felt his side were deserving of a greater advantage going into half-time.

A second Gibert penalty cut the lead to eight, but Munster had a great chance to take a more comfortable score into the break only to misfire at a key line-out with the final play of the half.

After surrendering a 21-point lead in the second half against Ulster last week, Munster will have needed no reminder about the need to finish the job here.

Any nerves over a potential repeat would have eased considerably only four minutes after the restart when captain Beirne rounded off a spell of pressure by crashing over the line from close-range.

But last week's failings were evident again as the opposition were allowed back into a game in which they had barely threatened previously.

Two tries in the space of seven second-half minutes cut Munster's lead to just three, with Hulleu scoring an opportunistic first for his side before replacement scrum-half Machenaud found himself in unfamiliar territory to finish off a close-range maul.

If Racing's bench initially lifted their performance, Munster got the desired impact from their replacements too with Wycherley's first involvement coming when Casey beautifully delayed a pass to put the lock through a gap and over the line.

But just as it looked like Munster were in the clear, Racing came back again.

Manu's try, which came after a slick interchange of passes with Hulleu and Sam James, was perhaps when Racing most looked like the team of old, but their efforts were quickly hampered by Roche's yellow for a clumsy collision with Munster full-back Ben O'Connor.

Against 14 men, Casey sniped over after breaking off the back of maul to score Munster's fifth of the night and finally secure the win.

The hosts will, however, again be looking for greater consistency across the 80 minutes when they return to United Rugby Championship action away to Leinster next weekend.

Munster: O'Connor; McCarthy, Nankivell, Kelly, O'Brien; O'Shea, Casey; Loughman, Van der Merwe, Aungier; Ahern, Beirne (c), Edogbo, Hodnett, Gleeson.

Replacements: Clein, J Wycherley, Brookes, F Wycherley, G Coombes, O'Donovan, Hanrahan, O'Donoghue.

Racing 92: Prisciantelli, Hulleu, Habosi, Manu, Tupou; Gibert, Latrasse; Njocke, Escobar, Kharaishvili; Lainault, Joseph, Tagitagivalu, Martins, Baudonne (c).

Replacements: Basse, Leota, Bamba, Hughes, Camara, Machenaud, James, Roche.

articles.title: Terzic: "Un partido un poco loco"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador lamenta la falta de acierto y muestra preocupación por la lesión de Guruzeta
articles.summary: El entrenador lamenta la falta de acierto y muestra preocupación por la lesión de Guruzeta
articles.body: El desenlace del Valencia-Athletic encontró un rápido análisis en las reflexiones de Edin Terzic. “Ha sido un partido un poco loco”, dijo el alemán en la sala de prensa de Mestalla. El preparador rojiblanco añadió que “si en el descanso me decís que no llevamos un punto hubiera dicho que no estoy de acuerdo porque ha habido más oportunidades. En la segunda mitad, sin embargo, ha sido diferente. Nadie ha merecido perder”. El técnico rojblanco lamentó algo que ya viene de atrás: la falta de definición de los suyo. “No hemos logrado acabar las jugadas, que ya es algo de lo que hemos hablado otras veces. Tenemos que mejorar en cuanto a las oportunidades. Nos han cubierto muy bien los huecos. Hay que mejorar en el tercio final del campo”, dijo. Terzic fue cauteloso con la lesión de Guruzeta, aunque las sensaciones no son las más optimistas posibles. “Lo de Guru quiza sea algo más serio, por respeto a él no me parece correcto pronunciarme. Veremos algo más al respecto en uno o dos días, cuando ya tenga todas las pruebas médicas realizadas”, comentó.

articles.title: Hibs: Marink Reedijk has 'sick feeling in stomach' - are his team in relegation fight?
articles.summary: Two games in, no points gathered and a chorus of boos greeting him at full-time at Easter Road. The honeymoon is well and truly over for Marink Reedijk.
articles.body:
Two games in, no points gathered and a chorus of boos greeting him at full-time at Easter Road... The honeymoon is well and truly over for Marink Reedijk.

Defeat in the new Hibs manager's opening two fixtures means the men from Leith have slumped to the bottom of the Scottish Premiership table.

It's left the Dutchman with what he described as "a strange feeling" in his stomach. So that begs the question: is his gut telling him his new side is now in a fight to avoid the drop?

With Halloween still a fortnight away, it may seem premature to drop the dreaded 'relegation' word into the Hibs conversation. But the fact the green half of Edinburgh is now looking up at the rest of the league a quarter of the way into the season is nonetheless cause for concern.

"I hate it," Reedijk told BBC Scotland after Saturday's 2-1 home defeat by Falkirk when asked about his side's place in the division. "It's something I don't want.

"I also think that based on today, we don't deserve it. But it's a fact and it's up to us to continue what we do, unpack the things we need to really work on, make sure these little mistakes don't happen and that we create momentum in our matches."

Hibs bottom after Falkirk mete out seventh home league defeat in row

Latest Hibs news, analysis and fan views

Get Hibs news notifications in the BBC Sport app

The 35-year-old took former club Beveren into the Belgian top flight on the back of an undefeated season last term. But his new side have won none of their last six in the league.

It's now over six months since Hibs celebrated a Premiership win in front of their own fans. Supporter patience, usually as rare as hens' teeth in football anyway, is in especially short supply around Easter Road these days.

"We need to work hard, stick to the things we do, develop the things we do, make sure that we make fewer and fewer mistakes and make sure that we take our chances," Reedijk said.

"I leave very disappointed with a strange feeling in my stomach because I think the guys worked their guts out. I think we deserved more, however we didn't get more. I'm therefore positive but with a sick feeling in my stomach."

Were there positive signs against Falkirk?

That sick feeling may take a while to dislodge.

Six home defeats from the club's last seven Premiership matches isn't on Reedijk. He's only been in the building a matter of weeks.

The task facing him, however, is culture change while winning. Tricky enough at the best of times but especially so when two of your next three games are against champions Celtic and arch-rivals Hearts in a national cup semi-final at Hampden.

Reedijk wants his side to dominate games. That happened, to a large extent, against Falkirk, with Hibs enjoying 70% possession.

It's what they do with the ball though that is their undoing at present. A failure to convert chances allied to individual errors. They had 17 shots to Falkirk's 10. Tellingly, the visitors had more on target: five compared to the hosts' three.

Reedijk can be encouraged by some of the other metrics: more entries into the final third (68 to 48); more touches in the opposition box (29 to 16); a higher tally of expected goals (1.35 to 0.76).

The only stat that matters to the external world however is a scoreline that leaves Hibs flailing at the wrong end of the table having taken a single point from the last available 18.

Under Reedijk's predecessor David Gray, Hibs enjoyed back-to-back top-six finishes for the first time since the late 2000s and were just minutes away from group-stage European football until a late collapse at home to Gent.

It was put to the former Hearts forward Ryan Stevenson that, right now, Hibs look a mess. "Yes, they do," he said on BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound.

"I don't know David Gray but I like David Gray. I know people say it came to a natural end but sometimes the grass is not always greener.

"They were better in the second half but did Falkirk ever really look like they were going to concede a goal? I don't think so.

"It's worrying, the fact that they're bottom of the league. It's still tight down there. It was a massive three points from Kilmarnock that's allowed them to go above Hibs. They need results fast."

Former Hibs midfielder Michael Stewart agrees but accepts finding those improved performances is not easy when the manager is still assessing his available options.

"There are a lot of questions that remain unanswered," he said on Sportsound.

"It feels a little bit like that at this moment where they're searching for something. Searching for a system. Searching for personnel. Searching for partnerships to evolve and bring them results.

"The new manager's in the door, he's got three massive games coming up, right on the back of two defeats."

Reedijk is adamant he sees positive signs and that there was improvement on the first performance under his watch at Dundee United last Saturday. That, too, ended in defeat.

The manager now has the dual task of keeping players and supporters alike onside while dragging the team away from the relegation zone. Hearts at Hampden also looms large on his horizon the day after Halloween.

The timescale to turn the Hibs tanker around could look a whole lot less scary if there's a national cup final to look forward to.

Michael: Hibs squad since we finished third has got progressively worse each transfer window as players leave and replacements are not made. Malky Mackay 100% needs to leave.

Colin: It's small margins that's costing us points. Cut out the individual errors and be more clinical and the manager will turn things around. He also needs the characters and leaders in the dressing room to step up.

Col: Garbage from start to finish, relegation fodder. Hibs have bigger problems than the players who can be sold/fired into space. The Gordons need to sell Hibs to someone who knows something about running a football club and move on.

Ringo: I said last week the players ain't good enough and again today they proved me right. These players got David Gray sacked. I'm 60 and I'd try harder than most of those players.

David: Malky Mackay needs to be the next one out of Easter Road. Ultimately he's the one to sign off on these signings as sporting director and the recruitment has been horrendous. These players don't have it in them and we are at serious risk of relegation come the end of the season.

Steven: This is one of the worst Hibs squads I've seen in a long time. They will get the new manager sacked by the end of the month.

articles.title: No. 4 Ohio State loses Julian Sayin, but stops No. 5 Indiana's 22-game win streak after Nick Marsh is barely out of bounds on go-ahead TD
articles.summary: The Big Ten clash turned out to be a defensive battle.
articles.body:
Indiana was oh-so-close to extending its win streak to 23 games.

Nick Marsh got wide open on a fourth down with just over a minute left, but was unable to stay in bounds on what would have been the go-ahead touchdown.

Just look at how close Marsh was to putting the No. 5 Hoosiers ahead on this pass from Josh Hoover. He knew right away that he might not have gotten his left foot down, though.

The win might have come at a significant cost, however. Ohio State QB Julian Sayin left the game in the second half after suffering an apparent right arm injury on a sack. Sayin ran back to the locker room gingerly holding his right arm, and returned to the sideline with his arm in a sling.

He was replaced for the rest of the game by freshman Luke Fahey.

Sayin did not have his best game before the injury. He was just 15-of-29 passing for 235 yards and threw two touchdowns to go along with two interceptions. But that second touchdown throw ended up being the game-winning score, when he threw up a long pass to Jeremiah Smith in the end zone.

The TD was Smith's first in three games against the Hoosiers. The Heisman favorite finished with four catches for 68 yards and the touchdown.

An extended absence for Sayin could be a big issue for an Ohio State team that travels to No. 19 USC after its Week 8 bye and then has Oregon, Northwestern and Nebraska before playing Michigan to end the season. As you'd expect, Fahey was a bit overwhelmed after replacing Sayin. He failed to complete either of his two pass attempts and took a sack.

A lot of things went against Indiana on Saturday

Not only was Marsh inches away from a game-winning score after his two long TD catches powered Indiana's Week 6 comeback against Nebraska, the Hoosiers lost fumbles on back-to-back possessions to start the second half.

Indiana hadn't lost a fumble in 1,437 offensive plays. It was a streak that dated back to the first game of that 22-game win streak that began in Week 1 of the 2025 season.

Kicker Nico Radicic missed a short field goal and then came up short on a 55-yard attempt. Were his two misses a reason why Indiana went for two after its second TD? After cutting Ohio State's lead to 19-13, Indiana didn't kick the PAT.

It was an inherently risky move. The failure to convert the 2-point attempt would have put the Buckeyes up nine — and two scores — with a field goal.

Hoover also appeared to suffer a right shoulder injury in the second half. He landed on his shoulder while scrambling and left the game for a play in obvious pain. He quickly returned to the field, but he was visibly grimacing after some throws.

The TCU transfer finished the game 20-of-40 passing for 296 yards. Much of that yardage went to Charlie Becker, who had nine catches for 165 yards.

The win should not derail Indiana's playoff hopes, especially as USC is the only ranked opponent remaining on the Hoosiers' schedule. Indiana plays at Michigan in Week 8 and then at home against Minnesota on Halloween before its bye week to begin November.

articles.title: Arsenal’s Heroic Comeback From 3-0 Down Against Bournemouth in 2017
articles.summary: The 2016/17 season saw Arsenal go on to win the FA Cup versus Chelsea 2-1 in May, for the 13th time in history, at the time a record for the most victories i...
articles.body:
The 2016/17 season saw Arsenal go on to win the FA Cup versus Chelsea 2-1 in May , for the 13th time in history, at the time a record for the most victories in the competition. However, there was one league game which stood out, showing the attacking prowess of the true Arsenal we know.

On 3 January 2017, Arsenal heroically fought back from three goals down to draw 3-3 versus AFC Bournemouth, who had only been in the Premiership for two seasons at the time, which feels incredible looking back on.

The Gunners had never dropped points against the Cherries in English top-flight history beforehand, beating them 3-1 in North London in their previous encounter during the 2016/17 campaign.

Bournemouth stun Arsenal with three goals

In the 16th minute at the Vitality Stadium, Eddie Howe's team took a shock lead after Charlie Daniels fired past Petr Cech, who had come frantically off his line (0-1).

Within four minutes, Callum Wilson doubled their advantage devastatingly from the penalty spot (0-2).

To make matters worse, Ryan Fraser stroked in the third and most brutal goal of the game just before the hour mark, forcing Arsenal to react as if they'd never gone a goal down originally (0-3).

Sanchez, Perez and Giroud inspire a heroic comeback

In the 70th minute, Alexis Sanchez, who would go on to become the Gunners' top goalscorer for the season with 30 strikes, commenced the comeback with a diving close-range header (1-3).

In the final third of the game, Lucas Perez, who had struggled to make an impact in an Arsenal shirt , made his impression at the right time, volleying an almighty effort from the left-hand side of the box (2-3).

With the dust looking to settle on the cards of defeat, our key striker throughout the 2010s, Olivier Giroud, ensured Arsenal escaped with some dignity to prevent one of the greatest Premier League upsets of all time, with a blitzing and classic header of his from the centre of the box (3-3).

What more could Arsenal have asked for but victory?

The Dorset side were far from the powerhouse they are now in England, featuring in Europe for the first time ever this season in the Europa League.

Following a rather intense 90 minutes of football, Arsene Wenger told BBC Sport that his side had passed a mental test of endurance:

"At the start we suffered from the quality of Bournemouth. One team had over three days to recover and on top of that we suffered at the back.

"It was a physical test but we came back into the game and we showed we are mentally strong."

Arsenal would go on to finish fifth that year, ending their long run of consecutive seasons in the Champions League. However, the Gunners still showed they were a team which demanded respect and admiration on certain occasions.

Gooners, what are your memories of Arsenal's remarkable comeback against Bournemouth in 2017? Was it one of the greatest fightbacks of the Wenger era? articles.title: All NFC North teams are above .500; Bears 5th-best NFC Playoff odds
articles.summary: The NFC North appears to be the NFL's most competitive division again.
articles.body:
The fickle nature of these SB Nation Reacts confidence polls are the same for all 32 fan bases. Our favorite team wins, and we're riding high. It's all sunshine and rainbows. But our favorite team loses, and the sky is falling. It's all doom and gloom.

A division loss just exacerbates the doom, and when it's the Green Bay Packers beating the Chicago Bears, the confidence poll drops from 94% of us believing the team is heading in the right direction to just 55%.

The NFC North is the only division where all four teams have winning records after five weeks, and this is the third straight year they've done that.

If the season ended today, all four NFC North teams would qualify for the seven-team playoff bracket.

Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the undefeated Minnesota Vikings with the second-best odds to make the NFC playoffs at -450.

The (3-2) Detroit Lions have the fourth-best odds at -178.

The (3-2) Bears, who are last in the division, have the fifth-best NFC postseason odds at -146, while the (3-2) Packers are ninth at +142.

The Bears are on the road to face the (2-3) Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, while the Packers host the (2-3) Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Minnesota and Detroit are on byes.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes dying after nasty loss to Florida | Golden
articles.summary: If you're still thinking Texas can run the table and still get into the CFP, you haven't been watching the Longhorns lately. What will Steve Sarkisian do now...
articles.body:
We knew as much about the Florida Gators coming into Saturday, but the Texas Longhorns provided visual evidence that the 2026 season will end for the second straight year with them on the outside looking in while the real national players compete for the College Football Playoff championship.

For those who are still holding onto the hope of Texas (4-2, 1-2) running the table to make the 12-team tournament, you haven't been watching. The Horns aren't very good at running anything these days, unless we're talking about running a season into the ground. It's over - not mathematically, but that will come soon enough, perhaps as soon as next Saturday against No. 9 Ole Miss or the following week against Mississippi State.

"We've got a better team that what we are right now," Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian said afterward.

Boos emanated from the fans at Royal-Memorial Stadium who stuck around to watch the Gators in victory formation. A second straight 27-24 loss to an unranked team - and the second straight loss to Florida, which ended up keeping Texas from last year's CFP - left them angry, frustrated and hurt, all at once.

Arch Manning's first lost fumble of the season was a killer. Texas' surprisingly porous defense had provided a late stop after the Longhorns had cut their 27-17 deficit to 27-24. Manning completed a 62-yard bomb to Emmett Mosley V on fourth-and-7 and then a 9-yard TD pass to Cam Coleman with 4 minutes, 21 seconds left.

The Horns can stop thinking about the CFP and just try to win a game. The offense produced a measly 272 yards on only 50 plays and went 2-for-10 on third-down conversions. Manning completed a pedestrian 14 of 20 attempts for 173 yards against the SEC's worst defense and remember, 62 of those came on one play.

The defense gave it up to Florida backup quarterback Tramell Jones and old Longhorns nemesis Jaden Baugh, and Sarkisian had zero answers for any of it. During the pivotal opening drive of the third quarter, Jones authored five straight third-down conversions against what was supposed to be an elite defense.

It all added up to a Sarkisian-coached team losing a second straight for the first time since his 5-7 debut in 2021.

"Everything will be evaluated," a visibly upset Sarkisian said.

When asked if that included the starting quarterback, Sarkisian said, "Everything is everything."

This has to go down as the worst loss since, well, last week's to the Oklahoma Sooners. Florida had been outscored 83-36 over the last two losses to South Carolina and Missouri.

"We haven't given up," Texas defensive tackle Hero Kanu said. "We still believe."

Now 1-2 in the toughest conference in America, the Horns are back at home against Ole Miss in their next one, which will feature a much better quarterback in SEC player of the year candidate Trinidad Chambliss.

Sarkisian should evaluate himself before he looks at any players. The Gators came in allowing 268 passing yards per game, the worst at defending the pass in the SEC, but he stuck to his bullet-less guns and decided against airing it out with talented pass catchers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman on the outside. And when the defense showed some cracks, the Horns - a roster that costs in the neighborhood of $45 million - were an open book.

These are the times that will test a team's mettle. Texas got out-toughed and outplayed by a team that showed tremendous belief.

And just like that, Texas' CFP future is very much on the line.

images.caption: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) is tackled during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman)

A Texas Longhorns fan reacts to a fumble recovery by Florida during the game at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman)

Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman)
